articles.title: 'Place national interest first': Opposition tells Nepal PM ahead of first India visit
articles.summary: Nepal's opposition Nepali Congress on Saturday urged Prime Minister Balendra Shah to prioritise national interest during his upcoming visit to New Delhi.
articles.body: Nepal's opposition Nepali Congress on Saturday urged Prime Minister Balendra Shah to prioritise national interest during his upcoming visit to New Delhi.Shah is set to embark on a two-day visit to India on Sunday, leading a 34-member delegation.Nepali Congress senior vice president Bishwa Prakash Sharma, in a statement, said the visit should serve Nepal's interests while further strengthening ties between the two countries.According to news agency PTI, the party said it had held internal discussions with subject-matter experts to offer the government constructive suggestions on areas of bilateral cooperation.The discussions covered climate change, air connectivity, tourism, trade, energy, sports, entrepreneurship, border management, concerns of people living in border areas, and challenges faced by Nepali workers in India, the statement said."Nepal-India relations should be grounded in mutual respect, sovereign equality, and national interest," the party said.As Shah is set to visit India representing Nepal, the Nepali Congress said broad consultations and a shared understanding on matters of national interest would strengthen the country's standing on the international forum.The party said it remained committed to protecting Nepal's interests and strengthening ties with its friendly neighbour India.The visit should focus on implementing commitments made in the past, resolving outstanding issues and laying the groundwork for long-term cooperation based on mutual benefit, it said.This will be Shah's first bilateral visit to any country since he assumed office on March 27. He travelled to the United States in September to attend the United Nations General Assembly.During the visit, Shah will call on President Droupadi Murmu and hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar will also pay a courtesy call on Shah, Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai told media persons at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Friday.Shah had received an invitation from Modi to visit India when the government led by the Rastriya Swatantra Party leader was formed in March, around six months after the youth-led Gen Z protests toppled the K P Sharma Oli government in September last year.You use AI every day.
